title: Exact rationalization and coherent scalar extension of coefficient-module complexes
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, fix an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\Ql$ in $\Qlb$, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For an arbitrary, possibly unbounded, cochain complex $N$ of $\mathcal O_E$-modules use termwise ordinary scalar tensors [def-weil-module-base-change] and derived categories defined by localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. There is a unique natural $L$-linear chain isomorphism
$$\beta_{L/E,N}:(N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}L\xrightarrow{\sim}(N\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E)\otimes_E L$$
whose degreewise value on pure tensors is
$$\beta_{L/E,N}((n\otimes a)\otimes b)=(n\otimes1)\otimes ab.$$
The inverse is the balanced map $((n\otimes x)\otimes b)\mapsto(n\otimes1)\otimes xb$ for $x\in E$, including fractions in the fraction field $E$ of $\mathcal O_E$. Both maps are independent of a fraction presentation. The functors $-\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$, $-\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$, $-\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}L$ and $-\otimes_E L$ are additive exact functors on modules, preserve quasi-isomorphisms termwise, and induce functors on the indicated derived categories. The isomorphism $\beta$ induces a natural isomorphism of these composite functors on $D(\mathcal O_E)$, natural also for arbitrary derived morphisms.

For $L=E$, $\beta_{E/E}$ is the identity under multiplication identifications. For finite $E\subset L\subset M\subset\Qlb$, put $Q_{G/F}(N)=N\otimes_{\mathcal O_F}\mathcal O_G$, $q_F(N)=N\otimes_{\mathcal O_F}F$, and $V_{G/F}(W)=W\otimes_FG$. On $(Q_{L/E}N\otimes_{\mathcal O_L}\mathcal O_M)\otimes_{\mathcal O_M}M$, the composite through $\beta_{M/E,N}$ after the integral tensor associator equals the composite through $\beta_{M/L,Q_{L/E}N}$, then $\beta_{L/E,N}\otimes_LM$, then the field tensor associator. This equality holds for chain complexes and in $D(M)$; on pure tensors all coefficient factors, including fractions, are multiplied in $M$.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_E$, $B=\mathcal O_L$. By [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], these are subrings of fields with the indicated compatible absolute values. For any nonzero $x\in E$, either $|x|\leq1$ or $|x^{-1}|<1$, so $A$ is a valuation ring in the precise sense of [lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat]; the same argument applies to $B$ in $L$. Also $E=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$: if $x\notin A$ then $x=1/x^{-1}$ with $0\ne x^{-1}\in A$. The analogous statement holds for $L$. The $A$-modules $B,E$, the $B$-module $L$, and the $E$-module $L$ are torsion-free because all their scalar inclusions are inclusions into fields. A field is itself a valuation ring. Apply [lem-trf-valuation-torsionfree-flat] to these four modules to obtain their flatness. No finite-generation hypothesis on a module is used. Lean implementation: extract the discrete valuation ring instance from Padic.extension_integers_dvr for the recorded subring. For every injective map from it to a domain, Module.isTorsionFree_iff_algebraMap_injective and Module.Flat over a Dedekind domain give flatness. Apply this to the restricted integer inclusion and both subtype maps. Field extension is flat by freeness.

source.place: Tag 0539, lemma-valuation-ring-torsion-free-flat; application to the coefficient subrings

proof.text: For each of the four flat scalar modules from step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] gives preservation of exact sequences and injections. Surjectivity after tensoring follows directly: lift the first entry of each pure tensor along a surjection, then add the lifts. Thus a short exact sequence remains short exact. The scalar-extension action on maps of [def-weil-module-base-change] is additive, since $(f+g)(n)\otimes c=f(n)\otimes c+g(n)\otimes c$. Kernels are preserved by applying exactness to $0\to\ker f\to P\to Q$, and cokernels by applying it to $P\to Q\to\operatorname{coker}f\to0$. Finite direct sums are preserved by the two inverse maps $(p,q)\otimes c\mapsto(p\otimes c,q\otimes c)$ and $(p\otimes c,q\otimes d)\mapsto(p,0)\otimes c+(0,q)\otimes d$, with their extensions by addition. The zero module is preserved. Consequently these additive functors preserve finite limits and colimits, as required for exact derived factorization. Lean implementation: the scalar-extension adjunction proves additivity and preservation of colimits. For arbitrary module size, apply Module.Flat.lTensor_exact to each short complex and Functor.exact_tfae to obtain finite-limit preservation; this does not require equating the ring and module universes.

source.place: Tag 00HD, lemma-flat; Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product: pure-tensor generation

proof.text: Fix an $A$-module $P$ and put $S=P\otimes_A L$. For $C=B$ or $E$, define $u_C:(P\otimes_A C)\otimes_C L\to S$ by $((p\otimes c)\otimes b)\mapsto p\otimes cb$ and $v_C:S\to(P\otimes_A C)\otimes_C L$ by $p\otimes b\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes b$. The tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] applies twice: the inner $A$-balancing is $(rp)\otimes cb=p\otimes rcb$, and outer $C$-balancing is $p\otimes(ca)b=p\otimes c(ab)$. For $v_C$, $((rp)\otimes1)\otimes b=(p\otimes r)\otimes b=(p\otimes1)\otimes rb$. Additivity in each variable is immediate. Both maps are $L$-linear, and $u_Cv_C(p\otimes b)=p\otimes b$, whereas $v_Cu_C((p\otimes c)\otimes b)=(p\otimes1)\otimes cb=(p\otimes c)\otimes b$. Generation by pure tensors proves they are inverse. Define $\beta_{L/E,P}=v_Eu_B$; its inverse is $v_Bu_E$, giving exactly both formulas in the statement. Lean implementation: use ModuleCat.extendScalarsComp for the two factorizations of the same map from O_E to L. Its forward map inserts one, and its inverse multiplies coefficients, as shown from extendScalarsComp_hom_app_one_tmul by linearity and tensor balancing. Their composite is the required module comparison.

source.place: Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product, universal property and bilinearity relations; explicit two-step balancing argument

proof.text: The preceding construction treats every $x\in E$ as an actual element of $L$. In particular, if $x=a/s=a'/s'$ with $a,a',s,s'\in A$ and $ss'\ne0$, then $as'=a's$ implies $ab/s=a'b/s'$ in $L$ for every $b\in L$. Thus the inverse formula gives the same element $p\otimes xb$ of $S$ and the same image under $v_B$ for either presentation. In the $E$-balanced target, $(p\otimes x)\otimes b=(p\otimes1)\otimes xb$, also for these fractions. There is no need to divide an element of $P$. Pure tensors span the iterated tensors by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], so the required formula determines $\beta$ uniquely. For an $A$-linear map $f:P\to P'$, both routes of the naturality square send $((p\otimes a)\otimes b)$ to $(f(p)\otimes1)\otimes ab$. Hence $\beta$ is natural on modules. Lean implementation: naturality is supplied by the two existing natural scalar-extension isomorphisms. Apply the two scalar-extension adjunction hom-equivalences to prove that equality on 1 tensor (1 tensor n) determines the entire module morphism. This gives uniqueness from the displayed generator formula.

source.place: Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product: balancing, generation, and uniqueness; fraction equality in the coefficient field

proof.text: Apply the module maps of steps 3 and 4 in each degree of $N$. Naturality for $d_N^r:N^r\to N^{r+1}$ gives the chain-map equations; the inverse maps obey the same equations. Naturality for each component of a chain morphism gives a natural $L$-linear chain isomorphism. For $L=E$, identify $N\otimes_A A$ with $N$ by multiplication, and $(N\otimes_A E)\otimes_E E$ with $N\otimes_A E$ in the same way. The formula sends $((n\otimes a)\otimes b)$ to $n\otimes ab$ under both identifications, so the comparison is the identity. These calculations use only degreewise maps and therefore apply to complexes unbounded in both directions. Lean implementation: NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex gives the unbounded chain comparison. Apply the same two adjunctions in every degree for chain uniqueness. The unit equation is checked on 1 tensor (1 tensor n), using the multiplication unit and the equality transport between the restricted identity map and RingHom.id.

source.place: Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product, applied degreewise; cochain conventions of def-weil-abstract-derived-category

proof.text: By step 2 each scalar functor satisfies all hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]: it is additive and preserves finite limits and colimits between module categories, which are abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian]. That node states that its termwise functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms, and supplies an induced functor with factorization through the cochain localization. Apply this to all four functors. Compose these factorizations to identify the restrictions of the two composite derived functors with the localization of the two composite cochain functors. Apply part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to the localized chain isomorphism of step 5. It yields a unique natural isomorphism between the composite derived functors with these components. Its naturality is for every arrow in $D(A)$, including inverses of quasi-isomorphisms; it is not merely natural for chain maps. Lean implementation: Functor.preservesQuasiIso_mapHomologicalComplex gives all four invariance statements. The comparison is the canonical mapDerivedCategorySquareIso of the ordinary comparison; mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fac and cancellation of the composition comparisons give precisely the specified descent square.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; localization of natural transformations as stated by the cited universal-property node

proof.text: For $E\subset L\subset M$, put $C=\mathcal O_M$. The integral associator sends $((n\otimes a)\otimes c)$ to $n\otimes ac$; the field associator has the identical multiplication formula. Their well-definedness and inverse follow from the $u_C,v_C$ balancing calculation of step 3, with the corresponding rings substituted. Evaluate the first tower route on $(((n\otimes a)\otimes c)\otimes d)$, for $a\in B,c\in C,d\in M$: integral association and $\beta_{M/E}$ give $(n\otimes1)\otimes(ac)d$. The second route first gives $((n\otimes a)\otimes1)\otimes cd$, then $((n\otimes1)\otimes a)\otimes cd$, and finally $(n\otimes1)\otimes a(cd)$. These agree by associativity in $M$. Here $d$ is any element of $M$, including a fraction; inserting any fraction from $L$ into an intermediate field tensor gives the same equality by its balancing relation. Pure-tensor generation proves equality in each degree and hence of chain maps. Lean implementation: apply the three scalar-extension adjunctions to reduce the ordinary tower equation to the generator 1 tensor (1 tensor (1 tensor n)). Both sides reduce by the coefficient formula and extendScalarsComp to 1 tensor (1 tensor n). This proves equality on arbitrary coefficients as well, since the adjunctions determine the entire morphism.

source.place: Tag 00CX, lemma-tensor-product; explicit multiplication calculation for both tower paths

proof.text: Apply the earlier exactness argument with the pairs $(E,M)$ and $(L,M)$ as well. The tensor associators in step 7 are natural module isomorphisms, so part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descends them just as in step 6. It respects identities and composition; whiskering is compatible as well, because after restriction along the localization each whiskered component is precisely the localized component evaluated on the termwise scalar complex. Therefore the restrictions of the two derived tower paths are the localized chain paths computed in step 7. Part (3) of that node makes the derived paths equal. The same argument descends the identity computation of step 5. This proves both coherence assertions in the derived categories with their specified factorization comparisons. Lean implementation: apply mapDerivedCategoryNatIso to the ordinary unit and tower equations. Its preservation of composition, compatibility with whiskering, and the unit and associativity laws for mapDerivedCategoryCompIso cancel the canonical comparison isomorphisms. These generic laws are proved in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.MapDerivedCategoryMate by localization faithfulness. Taking components proves the equations for every derived object.
